outcome: malignant ventricular arrhythmia (ventricular fibrillation, sustained ventricular tachycardia, or appropriate shock from an implantable cardioverter defibrillator)
cohort: The study included 18 high-risk women with arrhythmic mitral valve prolapse (AMVP) who experienced malignant ventricular arrhythmia and had at least one pregnancy.
finding: The perinatal period (pregnancy and up to 6 months postpartum) was associated with a significantly increased incidence rate of malignant ventricular arrhythmia compared to non-pregnancy periods in women with high-risk AMVP.
